text:
A Frost Advisory is in effect from 2 to 9 a.m. Thursday. Clear skies, dry air, and light winds will let temperatures fall quickly tonight, with a low around 44 and frost possible, especially away from the immediate waterfront. The sky is clear for the sunset that just passed, and the lake should stay quiet, with waves around 1 to 2 feet before winds go light. If you have sensitive plants, cover them tonight.

Thursday looks like a repeat of today, sunny and seasonable with a high near 67, though the models still differ by a few degrees. North winds stay light, and the lake should be especially manageable, with waves a foot or less. Plan on a crisp start, then an easy outdoor day, but protect plants before bed and take a jacket for the morning.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): Low 40°. A Frost Advisory is in effect from 2 a.m. to 9 a.m. Thursday for the northern St. Lawrence Valley, the Champlain Valley (outside Grand Isle County), and central and southern Vermont. Clear skies, light winds, and very dry air will support efficient overnight cooling, dropping valley temperatures into the mid-to-upper 30s. Widespread near-freezing temperatures will occur in central Vermont, the Northeast Kingdom, and the Adirondacks, with isolated cold spots in the Adirondacks dipping into the upper 20s. (Note: The NWS growing season program has officially ended for the Adirondacks and Northeast Kingdom, so formal advisories focus on central/southern Vermont, the Champlain Valley, and the St. Lawrence Valley). Frost will be less likely within 5 miles of Lake Champlain due to warmer lake waters. Patchy river fog is also expected late overnight.
